metadata.description: Single-plugin marketplace exposing the cc-enslaver discipline plugin.

plugins.name: cc-enslaver
plugins.description: A Claude Code plugin and LLM-agnostic rule pack that enforces systematic thinking, verified citations, and root-cause analysis — eliminating reactive, lazy AI behavior. v0.28.0 upgrades rules 03 + 09 into a mandatory trace-upstream → diagnose → unified-fix discipline: when a problem appears, point-to-point patching is banned outright. Rule 03 gains an upstream tracing ladder — every failure has a symptom site, a propagation path, and an origin (the mechanism / design decision / missing invariant that generates the bad state); fixing at the first two levels is a patch even when the observed failure disappears, climbing stops only with the true origin named and the reason stated, and the diagnosis must be demonstrated by a first-party probe / reproduction / failing test BEFORE the first line of the fix is written. Rule 09 gains 'one root cause, one unified fix' — a diagnosed root cause defines a CLASS of defects, the observed instance being merely the one that surfaced first; sweep the repo for every sibling, fix the generating mechanism once covering all instances in the same pass, and prove the class is closed by re-triggering at least one OTHER instance (N symptoms with one root = one fix, never N patches). Grounded in this repo's own measured history: v0.25.1 named a root cause and fixed only the instances it had seen, the mechanism survived and regenerated a fresh crop by v0.26 including one regression — v0.28 codifies v0.26's replace-the-mechanism response as the required shape of every fix. Zero new detectors, per the v0.22.1 precedent (a reasoning shape, not a syntax shape hooks can match); the existing hard layers — patch-marker content scan, rolling-patch frequency layer, Stop layer (f) root-cause triplet — remain the physical floor. A candidate Stop-layer marker extension is recorded for the user's decision rather than shipped unilaterally. Tests hold at 556. Prior — v0.27.0 closes the three items v0.26 recorded as 'known, not fixed' — deferring twice is how a documented limitation becomes permanent — and each direction was decided by evidence. FIRST, the shell tokeniser follows the SHELL rather than the host OS. v0.25.1 disabled backslash escaping when os.name == 'nt'; measuring the shell Claude Code actually runs on Windows (Git Bash / MSYS, bash 5.2.37(1)-release, OSTYPE=msys) showed that branch wrong in BOTH directions: the real shell eats an unquoted drive path's separators too, so it never rescued anything, and `git push --for\ce` arrives at git as --force while the guard saw a token it did not recognise — a live force-push bypass, now closed. Quoting is what preserves a drive path, in this tokeniser and in the shell alike; the register-hatch test that pinned the unquoted spelling was corrected to assert it does NOT register. SECOND, Stop layer (h) splits its verdict: 'attributable' is generous and drives PRESENCE (a false negative there blocks a reply for a tldr the author can plainly see and cannot diagnose), while 'countable' stays conservative and drives the 160-character MEASUREMENT. They differ only on CommonMark lazy continuation — the single-flag design is precisely why v0.26 skipped it, and it is implemented now. THIRD, Stop layer (i) requires one INFORMED answer per group: a sync marker settles only groups the session has actually been shown, because the primary path used to acknowledge every pending group while the grace path acknowledged only the presented set, and that inconsistency was itself the bypass (outlast the grace window, reach the looser path). A group is named by one block, then settled by the next reply. That is a deliberate strictness increase, not a defect fix. Tests 543 → 556. Prior — v0.26.0 was a fourth-round audit release that reviewed the PREVIOUS release's own fix diff and replaced the mechanism instead of the symptoms. Three parallel read-only reviews plus a first-party pass produced 37 findings; 33 were reproduced by first-party runtime probes, 3 recorded as by-design, 1 refuted. They collapse into three root causes. ALPHA — the detector encoded a SPELLING, not the concept: 'is this # a comment' was `line.find('#')`, which found the # inside a URL, so one neighbouring `https://api.example.com` line silenced the rule-10 SECRET detector outright (`example` is a rationale token and example.com is the IANA example domain); 'where does this try block end' was indentation over PHYSICAL lines, so a multi-line string re-anchored the block, and a handler suppressed every stack pop — which REGRESSED nested try/except from deny (v0.25.0) to allow (v0.25.1) while its own docstring claimed nesting was now handled; 'does this force-push' was words co-occurring in text, denying an echo of a force-push string and `git config alias.deploy "push --mirror"` while missing `git push origin +main`; 'is this token executed' was walking back over dashes, so `python -c register_read.py` polluted read state while `python -X utf8 …` (its own docstring's example) and `python3.13` were missed. Fixed by four shared models — lib/srclex (tolerant source lexer: comments vs docstrings vs data literals, string masking, bracket-joined logical lines), lib/mdctx (markdown fence/blockquote context, now consumed by BOTH halves of Stop layer (h), which previously disagreed about which fences count), lib/shellcmd (segments → argv → git subcommand / python script operand), and a schema-driven state normaliser. BETA — hardening scoped to the observed instance: v0.25.1's normaliser repaired `read_files` and left `session_id` raising KeyError (so a Read went unrecorded and the NEXT edit was falsely denied); auto-GC compared a raw session id against sanitised filenames; manage_edicts coerced only `id`. GAMMA — the claim outran the change: four tests passed unchanged on the pre-fix tree, and the self-rewritability invariant claimed to cover 'the whole tree' while globbing only hooks/scripts — SIX of the ten test modules were in fact self-locked. Also fixed: marker regexes now end at token boundaries (`# noquality`, `@ts-ignore-generated`, `eslint-disablement` were false DENIES), the rationale hatch accepts Chinese (因为 / 故意 — previously only the noun forms 原因 / 正当 were listed, so the natural verb form 因为 was rejected while English `because` passed, in a Chinese-primary repo) and block comments, and done-claim negation handles 'not yet done' / "isn't done" (the old `\bn't\b` was unreachable dead code). The fix was then RE-AUDITED before shipping, because the defect this release corrects was introduced by the previous release's fix. That pass found 8 more real defects in the NEW code, all fixed: `$( … )` / backtick / subshell invocations were not segmented — the text heuristic caught those by accident, so the model would have been a REGRESSION (`$(git push --force)` executes); an escaped triple-quote delimiter ended a docstring early, exposing string content as comments; three CommonMark bugs in the fence model (a closing fence with an info string closed its parent, `yaml-not` matched `yaml` by prefix, a 4-space-indented fence opened a fence); `cannot` / `unable` / `绝非` were missing from done-claim negation (the damaging direction — an honest 'not done' report gets blocked) while `not only fixed but tested` and the double negative `不得不承认已完成` were wrongly suppressed; and punctuation padding reached the rationale length bar. One change was REVERTED when it broke a deliberate v0.23 contract. Accepted as documented limitations: `//` inside a JS regex character class, a JS template literal's `${…}` interior, and an 8-level bound on blockquote peeling. Tests 378 → 543 across two audit rounds; the first round's 43 failures + 3 errors replay on the pre-fix tree. A SECOND round of 16 parallel read-only reviews (15 reported; the sync-gate lens returned nothing and is recorded as NOT RUN rather than counted) fixed 20+ further confirmed defects at the root: a bare triple-quoted expression counted as a docstring, so `"""because …"""` dropped anywhere silenced the secret detector; a lone CR let a `#` comment swallow the rest of the file; the tldr length check skipped the attribution test on CONTINUATION lines, measuring a blockquoted line as the agent's own — the two-halves-disagree bug this release created lib/mdctx to end, recurring one level down; `far from done` parsed as a completion claim and BLOCKED an honest failure report, while a Chinese double negative anywhere in the clause disabled a nearer real negation; `Work complete` matched no done-pattern and therefore skipped all nine Stop layers; a JSONDecodeError reset session state to empty and the next mutator saved it back, silently erasing every read, baseline and counter; the six static Bash patterns still matched raw text while force-push had a parse model, so `chmod -v 777` and `git -C . rebase --skip` were missed and `echo git commit --no-verify` was wrongly denied; and a registration inside `false && …` earned read credit for a command the shell never executes. The doc gate's own holes were closed too — and it had exempted the CURRENT release's narrative as 'history' while that narrative describes the release being shipped, which is how five stale `378 → 474` statements and two false claims about this release survived a green gate. Second-round assertions were NOT replayed on a pre-fix tree, because both rounds are uncommitted and no such tree exists; that limitation is stated rather than glossed. Prior: three parallel read-only reviews of the v0.25.0 tree returned 94 findings, 21 were reproduced by first-party runtime probes, and those 21 collapse into SIX root causes — fixed as six systematic changes rather than 21 patches. Red-first regressions 350 → 378, of which 37 failures + 4 errors replay on the pre-fix tree. Theme: detectors that described a STRING instead of a CONCEPT. Nine findings were one spelling away from the pattern — CRLF defeated all five single-line rule-09 markers (on this plugin's primary platform); any trailing text made a marker invisible, so `@ts-ignore` + a bare deferral keyword was allowed while the bare form was denied, and the rationale check never ran at all; a comment line between `except:` and `pass` moved the swallow out of the scanner's sight, leaving rule 09's escape hatch unreachable for its most natural spelling (v0.25 fixed the same-line variant and shipped a regression test that passed for the wrong reason); `except Exception: pass` one-liners, nested calls in `time.sleep(max(0, d))`, doubled backslashes in `"C:\\Users\\bob"` (how a user-home path actually appears in committed source), `git -C repo push --force`, quoted `"--force"`, `+refspec` and `--mirror` all slipped past. Second root cause: untrusted TOML values used without a type check — `severity = ["must"]` and `mode = []` are valid TOML and raised `TypeError: unhashable type` out of loaders documented as never raising, disabling rules 04 + 08 for a whole session and taking Stop layer (i) with them. Third: the rationale escape hatch was wrong in both directions — honored inside arbitrary code (`reason = compute()` silenced an adjacent marker) yet unreachable as a standalone comment. Fourth: presence checks standing in for meaning — `已完成` / `Implemented` / `Finished` were not in DONE_PATTERNS, so ALL nine Stop layers were skipped, while `Not done; tests failed.` counted as a completion claim; an empty `tldr:` satisfied layer (h) outright. Fifth: auto-GC could delete the live session's state on resume, and a mistyped GC marker suppressed the entire SessionStart injection. Sixth: a grace-window sync ack silenced groups the agent was never shown. Prior: v0.25 second-round audit (12 fixes, 7 HIGH); v0.24 health audit (10 fixes, 3 HIGH); v0.23 rule 12 repo-wide sync + 160-char TL;DR cap; v0.22 rules 10 + 11 content detectors. English is the i18n skeleton and source of truth (rules/ + prompts/ at the root, default injection); Chinese is a first-class translation (rules/zh/ + prompts/zh/, CC_ENSLAVER_LANG=zh), with drift CI-blocked by i18n_check.py + test_i18n_sync.py.
